day_local: Ulluriaq Uqqujiutiktuq Sanningajumik (Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross)
greeting: Ataniup atianik, Ataataup, Irniup, ammalu Anirniup Salumajuup. Ullaakkut, ilinnut tamainnut, Ataniq Jiisusi Kristusiup sanningajua quviasugutigiingniarparput.
penitential:
Ataniq, ungasiktumik inuusiqarnirput tuqsuungniarpiuk. 
Kristusi, uummativut saalulugu. 
Ataniq, nalliginiarpiutigut, inuusiqarnirput nutaanguqtillugu.
psalm_response: Do not forget the works of the Lord!
homily:
In the desert, the people were tired. Their feet were sore from the sand, their throats were parched, and their patience—that thin, fragile thread that holds us together when the journey is long—had finally snapped. They looked at the manna, that daily gift of bread from heaven, and they called it 'wretched.' It is a human thing to do, isn't it? When the ache of the journey becomes too much, we stop seeing the gift and start seeing only the hunger. We stop seeing the providence and start seeing only the emptiness. The people complained, and in their bitterness, they lost their way. They were bitten by serpents, and in that moment of sting and shadow, they had to look up. They had to look at the bronze serpent on the pole—not because the metal had power, but because their obedience in looking was an act of turning back to God. They had to lift their eyes from the dust of their own misery to the sign of their salvation. 

I want you to think about that image of looking up. Think about how much of our lives we spend looking down. We look down at the floor when we are overwhelmed. We look down at our screens, at our worries, at the things we cannot fix. We look down at the heavy, quiet spaces where we wish a voice would break the silence. But today, the Church holds up the Cross. It is the ultimate 'looking up.' It is the moment when the Son of Man is lifted high, not to show us a tragedy, but to show us the depth of a love that refused to stop at the edge of death. 

Benjamin knew something about looking up. You have told me how he loved to watch the airplanes, how he would stand there, head tilted back, eyes tracking the flight path of a Boeing 737 across the blue. There was a wonder in him that wasn't tied to the ground. He was a boy who lived with his eyes on the horizon, always curious, always dreaming of what was next—even when he was just standing on a porch in his flip-flops, gazing out toward the driveway. He had that rare, beautiful capacity to see beyond the ordinary. He didn't just see a jet; he saw a possibility. He didn't just see a math problem; he saw a logic that connected the world. And that is exactly how we are called to look at the Cross today. We are called to look past the wood, past the suffering, and see the 'Con Chim Airlines' of the soul—the way God has cleared the flight path for us to reach the Father’s house. 

There is an ache in this room, and I will not pretend it isn't there. The empty chair, the morning light that feels too bright when you are carrying a heavy heart, the nights when the silence seems to have a weight of its own—these are real. They are the 'desert' parts of your journey. But the Gospel today gives us a promise that is meant to travel with you into those quiet, difficult hours. 'For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.' Think about that 'gave.' It wasn't a transaction. It was an offering. It was the Father saying, 'I love you so much that I will hold nothing back.' 

Benjamin understood the heart of an offering. Remember that moment with his piggy bank? He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it, and he didn't need to hand it over. The act of offering was what mattered. It was his way of saying, 'I am with you, Uncle. I am here.' He offered his entire world because he loved. And in that, he was reflecting the very heart of the Father. When you feel the weight of your loss, when you feel like you have nothing left to give, remember that you are part of a love that has already given everything. You are not alone in your offering. You are held by the One who gave His Son for you. 

I speak to you now, Alan and Thao, and to you, Ryan. I know the nights are long. I know the memories of the family trips—the Áo Dài with the golden dragons, the laughter on the rocks, the simple joy of a shared meal—sometimes feel like a beautiful, distant country you can no longer visit. But the Cross tells us that the distance is not as great as it seems. Because of the Cross, the horizon is open. Benjamin is not in the past; he is in the presence of the One who is the Alpha and the Omega. He is, as you said, at the Banquet. He is in the light. And the same Jesus who was lifted up on the Cross is the one who is sitting with you at your table today. He is the one who hears every 'Mẹ' whispered in the dark. He is the one who understands the bond between brothers, because He Himself is the Brother of us all. 

Do not let your hearts be hardened by the desert. Do not let the silence of the house make you forget the voice that once filled it with giggles and dreams of aviation. That life—that brilliant, gentle, curious life—was a gift that has not been taken away; it has been returned to the Source of all light. Benjamin’s life is a testament to the fact that love is not a finite resource. It is a well. Just like the 'Giếng Gioan Baotixita' that flows in his name, his love continues to nourish, to sustain, and to give life to others. Your love for him is doing the same. Every time you speak his name, every time you remember his smile, every time you choose to keep living with the same courage and curiosity he had, you are letting that well flow. 

So, what do you carry out the door? Today, when you feel that sting of the serpent—that sudden, sharp reminder of the loss—do not look down. Do not look at the bite. Look up. Look at the Cross. Remember that the journey is not about the desert; it is about the destination. Look up and see the sky, just like Ben used to do. See the airplanes, the birds, the vastness of the blue, and know that your son is soaring. He is free. He is home. And he is waiting for you to join him at the gates of the Father’s house. 

Live for him, Ryan. Study, play, dream, and look at the world with that same brilliant, questioning mind. You are his brother, and that is a bond that even death cannot touch. Alan and Thao, keep your hearts open. You have loved well, you have loved perfectly, and that love is the bridge that will keep you connected to him until the day the, as the Gospel says, 'everyone who believes in him might not perish but might have eternal life.' 

Today, take a small, simple step. When you see a plane in the sky, or when you sit down to rest, simply whisper, 'Thank you, God, for the gift of Benjamin.' And then, breathe. Breathe in the peace of the One who was lifted up for you. You are held. You are loved. And you are never, ever walking this road alone.
standing_petitions: Benjamin Vo ammalu tamaita inuujunnaqtut, Ataniup qaumanianni inuujunnaqtut, irnitsiaraluarlutik.
Tamaita uqumaittumik aaniarniqartut, Ataniq qaisimajauqqujauvut, niriungniqarnirmik ammalu qanuinnginnirmik tunijauqqujauvut.
spiritual_communion: Jiisusi, niriukpunga ilvit sanningajumi, ammalu uummatinniittutit. Niriukpunga ilvit iluaniittunga, ammalu ilvit iluaniittunga. Aulaniqtuq, takujaujunnaqtutit, uummatinniittutit. Amen.
closing: Ataniq Jiisusi Kristusiup nalliginiarninga, ammalu Ataataup asujininga, ilissinniittuli. Amen.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text: With their patience worn out by the journey, the people complained against God and Moses, 'Why have you brought us up from Egypt to die in this desert, where there is no food or water? We are disgusted with this wretched food!' In punishment the LORD sent among the people saraph serpents, which bit the people so that many of them died. Then the people came to Moses and said, 'We have sinned in complaining against the LORD and you. Pray the LORD to take the serpents from us.' So Moses prayed for the people, and the LORD said to Moses, 'Make a saraph and mount it on a pole, and if any who have been bitten look at it, they will live.' Moses accordingly made a bronze serpent and mounted it on a pole, and whenever anyone who had been bitten by a serpent looked at the bronze serpent, he lived.

readings.label: Reading 2
readings.text: Brothers and sisters: Christ Jesus, though he was in the form of God, did not regard equality with God something to be grasped. Rather, he emptied himself, taking the form of a slave, coming in human likeness; and found human in appearance, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to death, even death on a cross. Because of this, God greatly exalted him and bestowed on him the name that is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Jesus said to Nicodemus: 'No one has gone up to heaven except the one who has come down from heaven, the Son of Man. And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life.' For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him might not perish but might have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but that the world might be saved through him.

day: Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
Hey Ben,  nếu có thể hãy cho anh Minh gặp Ben trong giấc mơ nhé, dù chỉ là lời chào hay nụ cười như cách Ben vẫn hay tạo dáng để chụp hình. Nhớ và thương Ben nhiều lắm

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - need a miracle here. We miss you so much and we’re not sleeping much. Ryan wish you were here, especially this upcoming Saturday to play the new version of Project Flight with him.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Dear Ben, our uncle Thanh has passed away. Please watch over him and pray that his soul finds peace. His saint name is Phêrô. Lord, thank you for sending Chu Thanh into my life. I'll always be grateful for the time he spent tutoring me in math back in high school
